She possesses great splendor and the goddess Lakṣmī; she has the radiance of ten million suns, five faces, ten arms, and is endowed with fifteen eyes.
The great goddess of white complexion, the Great Preta, is seated in the midst of the eight Mothers; she is the Yoginī of Accomplishment, who is worshipped.
The world is made to blaze by the licking flames issuing from her opened mouth;
by the force of her exhalations and inhalations, she causes even the great mountain ranges to tremble.
In some places it is in a house, in some places in a hut; in some places it withdraws from that which is moving.
In some places she creates, in others she protects; independent and pure, she proceeds.
Adorned with all remaining ornaments and seated upon a throne supported by elephant-headed lions,
the Goddess holds a noose and a goad, with her hands granting boons and fearlessness.
3b) Holding a sword in his left hand, he causes the trembling of the three worlds;
in his left [other] hand an extremely fierce khaṭvāṅga, and in his right an excellent trident.
He should place in his left hand a fierce skull-bowl smeared with blood, worshipped and filled with the blood of a severed head.
In her left hand, however, she holds a divine flask filled with great jewels;
this is the goddess Pratyaṅgirā, whose body dwells in the supreme sky.
Pervading the universe through both singular and manifold divisions, she remains established.
The great goddess Pratyaṅgirā is the fortune of accomplishment who bestows victory.

O Goddess who is the supreme swan (*paramahaṃsinī*), the goddess who bestows the path to *nirvāṇa*, the pacifier of all calamities, the destroyer of all misfortunes, evils, and afflictions, she whose feet tread upon the ocean, the subduer of all enemies—Goddess, come! Come! Laugh! Laugh! Roar! O you who drink human blood, fat, and marrow, crush the enemy hosts! Crush them! Eat them! With your trident!
Split! Split! Cut! Cut! Strike with the sword! Destroy! Destroy!

Thus concludes the worship of the argha vessel. Self-worship: Aiṃ, ointment and sandals. Aiṃ 5 Hrīṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ, the three principles (tritatva), Hrūṃ, field (kṣetra) and sandals. Aiṃ 5 Śrīṃ.
